Bar numbers — the drawing

Four sections, each plate at true size and again at three and a half times. The staff, clef, key signature, notes, stems, beams, underlay, tacet mark and tuplet bracket in every plate are the production renderer’s real output, captured from the running app’s DOM at 1400 × 900 on the engraved Without Sun song 1, at the production stave of 5.5 px. The bar numbers are not. Ilya draws no bar number anywhere, so this page draws them, at the geometry each plate’s label states. Nothing here is built and nothing here is proposed.

What is settled before you look: the first measure of every system takes a number, the first bar of the piece does not, the number sits above the clef at the system’s left edge, it is italic, and it carries no box or circle. Those are your rulings of 2026-08-29 and Gould p484-a, p484-c, p484-d and p484-e, read in gould-bar-numbers-p484_2026-08-29.md. Size, weight, clearance and horizontal anchor are what Gould does not give and what these plates are for.

A. Size and weight of the italic number, above the clef

The system is measures 12 to 14 of the engraved song, whose first measure is source m. 13, so the number is 13. The number is centred on the clef’s ink, which runs 27.75 to 43.33, and its baseline is held at 1.0 stave-space above the top staff line through the whole section, so only size and slope vary. The fourth plate is this desk’s addition: the section varies weight and the brief’s table gives no weight plate, so there is one semibold at the middle size. Ignore it if it is not wanted.

B. Clearance, and the horizontal anchor of the post-rest number

The system is measures 12 to 16 of the same song with the vocal notes stripped from source measures 14 to 16, which is what makes a three-bar tacet run inside a system. The measure after the run is source m. 17, so the number is 17. That number has no clef beneath it, which is the open question the system-start number does not have. The three anchors are the run’s closing barline at x = 362.95, the first notehead’s ink centre at x = 380.84, and the midpoint at x = 371.89. Every number here is centred on its anchor.

C. The post-rest number, bare against parenthesized

You called the post-rest number “a useful courtesy”, 2026-08-29. The courtesy accidental’s own convention is a parenthesis, and r178 p.490 parenthesizes a continuation system’s number for a related reason. Not ruled. The bare number is drawn at the split anchor. The parenthesized one is drawn at all three of section B’s anchors, because the width a parenthesis costs interacts with where the number sits. All four are 2.0 stave-spaces at 1.0 stave-space of clearance.

parenthesized, anchor split

D. The crowded band

One real system carrying all of it at once: the bar number 13 above the clef, the tacet count 3 over the consolidated rest, the post-rest bar number 17, and the tuplet count 2 over source m. 17. The tacet count and the tuplet count are the renderer’s; the two bar numbers are this page’s. The tuplet count is already italic at 11 px (staff-renderer.ts:1118, pinned by a test at staff-renderer.test.ts:290), so an italic bar number shares a face and a slope with it. Gould separates the two by position rather than by face. This plate is where that either holds or does not.

Built 2026-08-29 for N.104’s successor ruling. Self-contained: Finale Maestro, Lato IPA and Source Serif 4 are embedded as data URIs and nothing here loads from the network. Source Serif 4 is the face the page’s own text is set in, and it is what the tuplet count already renders in, so the bar numbers are drawn in it too. Nothing in this file is built into Ilya and nothing in it is a proposal.
